before.source_text: Induction on $n$. Take a real unit eigenvector $q_1$. The subspace $q_1^\perp$ is mapped into itself, since $q_1^\top Ax=(Aq_1)^\top x=\lambda_1q_1^\top x=0$ for $x\perp q_1$. There $A$ is again symmetric, so by induction it has an orthonormal eigenbasis $q_2,\dots,q_n$. Distinct eigenvalues are never needed; for a repeated one any orthonormal basis of its eigenspace works, so $Q$ is not unique.
